sutta: 4.7 On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rajagaha, the bamboo grove, the squirrel sanctuary. Then when the night was fading, the blessed one, having spent much of the night walking back and forth in the open, washed his feet, entered his dwelling, and lay down on his right side in the lion's posture, with one leg overlapping the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, having attended to the idea of rising. Let's stop here for a moment. You see, uh, Buddha and his among disciples, as you see here, when the night was fading, the blessed one having spent much of the night walking back and forth in the open. The night uh starts at about 6:00 p.m. So, when the night was fading, uh probably it would be around uh the first at the end of the first watch, about 10:00 p.m. uh. So, the the Buddha spends much of the night walking back and forth. Uh most of us, uh when the night comes, uh we feel exhausted. We want to lie down and take a rest. But the Buddha and his disciples, uh they try to maintain their wakefulness for as long as possible until they are totally exhausted. They cannot stand that. Only then they lie down. This practice of maintaining the wakefulness in Pali is called Jagariya No Yoga. On the word jaga, it means jaga mindfulness. Then, uh I see the Buddha, he when he lies down, he lies down on his right side in the lion's posture. Chinese you call what? Su Tzu Wo. Mhm. Lying on the right side. One leg overlapping the other. You see here, mindful and clearly comprehending. Sati Sampajanna. That means, even when the Buddha and his among disciples, when they lie down, they don't fall asleep. They still practice sati, they still practice sampajanna, they are still mindful. And they are still uh remembering their meditation sub- subject, sati, remembering your meditation subject. So, like if they're meditating on the breath, now, even he lies down also, huh, he still watch the breath. Try not to fall asleep. Then Mara, the evil one, approached the Blessed One and addressed him in verse. One, you sleep. Why do you sleep? What's this? You sleep like a wretch. Thinking the hut's empty, you sleep. What's this? You sleep when the sun has risen. And the Buddha said, "Within him craving no longer lurks, and tangling and binding to lead him anywhere. With the destruction of all acquisitions or attachments, the awakened one sleeps. Why should this concern you, Mara?" Then Mara, the evil one, disappeared right there. So, you see, um And Mara is always coming to disturb the Buddha. But once the Buddha sees that the Buddha recognizes him, huh, then he will go away.
